title: Sprich on an M4 Pro Mac with 24 GB: Local Dictation That Types Into Any App
dek: A first session on 9 November 2026: a polished five-step setup, quick dictation in English and German once the tester used the key correctly, a German-only interface, and most side features not tried.

seo.title: Sprich Hands-on Test: Local Dictation on an M4 Pro Mac
seo.description: Hands-on test of Sprich on a 24 GB M4 Pro Mac: dictation worked in Word, WhatsApp and Telegram in English and German, Russian failed.

faq: Does Sprich work in other apps?
Yes, in the apps the tester tried. Dictation produced text in Microsoft Word, WhatsApp and Telegram. Mail, Notes, Slack and a browser were not tried.
Which languages did Sprich handle in the test?

English and German worked. A French sentence was dictated and its text is in the notes, but accuracy was not judged. A Russian test failed: the output was garbled. The dictation language set at that time is not recorded.
Is Sprich’s interface available in English?

No. The tester found only a German interface and no language switch. The developer says it is German only so far, a deliberate choice because the local version is optimised for German; that is not verified.
How big is the Sprich download?

Setup downloads two models, Sprich Transcribe v3 (about 480 MB) and Sprich Turbo v3 (about 2.8 GB), about 3.3 GB together by the app’s own text. These are download sizes; runtime memory was not measured.
Does Sprich really run offline and locally?
The app says everything runs locally, that voice and text never leave the Mac and that it works fully offline. Network traffic was not inspected and no offline run was tried, so this is not verified.

The tester first judged it slow because he used the default toggle mode wrongly (press once, speak, press again). After correct use he found it instant and as fast as his cloud dictation tool. Nothing was timed.

verdict.general: A carefully built, German-first dictation app for Apple Silicon Macs. In this session dictation worked in Word, WhatsApp and Telegram in English and German; Russian did not. Meeting recording, file transcription, text rewriting, offline operation, the privacy claims and uninstall were not tested.
verdict.fit: The tester is impressed, gives it five out of five and recommended it to a contact. He rates it as fast as his cloud dictation tool, though nothing was timed. Whether he will keep using it is not stated in his notes.

chapters.title: Download, first launch and setup
items: The test ran on 9 November 2026. The tester downloaded a small DMG, which he read as 20 MB; no screenshot. The installer window shows the app icon beside an Applications shortcut. The directory lists 18.2 MB for version 2.2.4 (third-party).
The tester likes the logo, a German play on the word Sprich split into “spr” and “ich”.
An account is needed: setup step 1, “Anmelden”, is ticked before the model step, and the tester says registration is required.

Step 2 downloads two models once: Sprich Transcribe v3 (speech recognition, about 480 MB) and Sprich Turbo v3 (text improvement, about 2.8 GB), about 3.3 GB together by the app’s own text. The download runs in the background while the next steps are done. These are download sizes, not runtime memory.
The screens do not name the models underneath. The tester noticed this and wanted to find out.

He changed the dictation key; which key he chose is not recorded. Step 4 shows Fn, while the welcome screen’s illustration shows right Command. Two modes exist: Einrasten (press to start, press to stop; marked Standard) and Gedrückt halten (record while held).
He reached the last step, “Fast geschafft”, while the models were still downloading: speech recognition 72 %, text improvement 12 %. Total download time and setup time are not recorded.

chapters.title: Usage
items: The first Word tests felt slow and one text seemed to go missing. The tester wrote that a speech tool has to answer within a second or two and that his cloud tool was faster. Then he found his own mistake: in the default toggle mode the key has to be pressed once to start and once to stop. He corrected the notes.
With the key used wrongly, the tester estimates several seconds, sometimes over 10 s, before text appeared. After correct use he found the app instant. Nothing was timed.

The first four English dictations into Word, 17:43 to 17:49, are 7 to 13 words each. One reads “Sprich Ae” in the history where the tester’s notes show “Sprich AI”; what he said and whether he edited the text are not recorded.

German dictation into WhatsApp arrived with greeting, paragraphs and punctuation, and the tester says it sorted the text correctly. One phrase, “die doppelt drücken knüpfen muss”, reads oddly; the intended wording is not recorded.
English dictation into Telegram arrived as three messages with filler words such as “Uh” kept. The setup screen promises correction of punctuation, capitalisation and recognition errors, not fillers.

A French sentence was dictated and its text is in the notes; the tester did not judge accuracy and the spoken sentence is not recorded. A Russian test did not work: the app did not understand the words and the output was garbled. The language setting at that time is not recorded; that it was set to German is an inference.

The History tab kept every dictation with time, target app, text, recording length, word count and saved time, plus a search box and an app filter. At 17:49 the headline said 41 s saved this week and the tile 56 s; at 18:07 (32 transcriptions, 676 words) the headline said 12 min 23 s and the tile 19 m. The app does not explain how “saved” is computed.
Later he switched to hold-to-talk, the mode he is used to, and was impressed again. Not timed.

chapters.title: Settings, extras and the developer’s reply
items: A popup menu offers Änderung beschreiben, Korrekturlesen, Umformulieren, Freundlich, Sachlich, Kompakt, Zusammenfassung, Hauptpunkte, Liste, Tabelle and Verfassen. The tester wanted to understand how it works and did not use it. Which program provides the menu, Sprich or macOS, is not recorded.
Settings has a Schreibton dropdown, Formal (ticked) or Informell. Only the dropdown was seen; the tester’s “Wow” is about the option, not a tested result.
The recording indicator can be set to Taste, Mikro (selected) or Kein. The tester saw a microphone bubble change from grey to orange; the header shows “Mikro bereit”.

The sprich.ai account page offers a password change and two-factor authentication. The tester was “really impressed” by the latter, but the card shows only an “Aktivieren” link, so it was not switched on.

The Meetings tab offers “Meeting aufnehmen”; its tip says calls give a transcript, summary and tasks and everything stays on the Mac. The tester has not recorded a meeting and plans to try it with a few people in a room.
He looked for a language switch to make English screenshots and found none; the interface is German only.

The built-in “Bug melden” form has Bug, Feedback and Feature tabs and fields for title, description, expected and actual result, frequency and up to 3 attachments of 1 MB each. The “Mitgesendete Daten” section was not opened and whether anything was sent is not recorded. “Transcripts are never sent” is the form’s own line.

The developer replied to the tester in German after the test; the date is not stated. Paraphrased: he is glad the tester now makes his recordings with Sprich; Parakeet understands about 25 European languages, selectable for file transcription; dictation is optimised for German, and English terms inside a German sentence work well; the interface is German only so far, a deliberate choice because the local version is optimised for German. None of this is verified.

findings: The tester read the DMG download as 20 MB; no screenshot. The installer window shows the app icon beside an Applications shortcut. The directory's own check on the same day lists 18.2 MB for version 2.2.4 (third-party).
An account is needed: setup step 1, "Anmelden", is ticked before the model step, and the tester says registration is required.

Setup downloads two models once: Sprich Transcribe v3 (speech recognition, about 480 MB) and Sprich Turbo v3 (text improvement, about 2.8 GB), about 3.3 GB together by the app's own text. The download runs in the background while the next steps are done. These are download sizes, not runtime memory.

The screens name only "Sprich Transcribe v3" and "Sprich Turbo v3"; the models underneath are not named. The developer names Parakeet and about 25 European languages; the PromptQuorum directory lists 57 languages (third-party). Neither figure was verified and they do not agree.

Setup step 5, "Fast geschafft", appeared while the models were still downloading (speech recognition 72 %, text improvement 12 %) and says dictation starts when they finish. Total download time and setup time are not recorded.

The dictation key can be changed and the tester changed it; which key he chose is not recorded. Setup step 4 shows Fn, while the welcome screen's illustration shows right Command ("⌘ Rechts"); which is the default and which he set is not recorded. Two modes exist: Einrasten (press to start, press to stop; marked Standard) and Gedrückt halten (record while held).

In the default toggle mode the tester used the key wrongly and read the result as a slow app: tester-estimate several seconds, sometimes over 10 s before text appeared. After correct use he found it fast. The instruction is on screen twice, in German. That a default toggle differs from the hold-to-talk habit of many users is an assumption.

After the mistake the tester judged dictation "instant" and, in a message to a contact, as fast as his online dictation app, which is not named. No delay was timed; the history shows recording length and time saved, not latency.

English dictation into Word produced four history entries of 7 to 13 words. One reads "Sprich Ae" in the history where the tester's notes show "Sprich AI"; what he said and whether he edited the text are not recorded.

German dictation into WhatsApp arrived with greeting, paragraphs and punctuation; the tester says it sorted the text correctly (tester-view). One phrase, "die doppelt drücken knüpfen muss", reads oddly; the intended wording is not recorded.

English dictation into Telegram arrived as three messages with filler words such as "Uh" kept. The setup screen promises correction of punctuation, capitalisation and recognition errors, not fillers, so this is not a miss against it.
A French sentence was dictated and its text is in the notes. The tester did not judge accuracy and the spoken sentence is not recorded.
A Russian test "got lost" by the tester's account: the app did not understand the words and the output was garbled. The spoken phrase and the dictation language at that time are not recorded.

A History tab lists every dictation with time, target app, text, recording length, word count and saved time, plus a search box and an app filter. The tester likes that the texts are kept and sees it as a way to retrieve everything he dictated (tester-view).
The saved-time figures disagree on the same screen (see the numbers table). The app does not explain how "saved" is computed or what each figure covers.

A popup menu offers Änderung beschreiben, Korrekturlesen, Umformulieren, Freundlich, Sachlich, Kompakt, Zusammenfassung, Hauptpunkte, Liste, Tabelle and Verfassen. The tester wanted to understand how it works and did not use it. Which program provides the menu, Sprich or macOS, is not recorded.
Settings has a Schreibton dropdown, Formal (ticked) or Informell. Only the dropdown was seen; the tester's "Wow" is about the option, not a tested result.
The recording indicator can be set to Taste, Mikro (selected) or Kein. The tester saw a microphone bubble change from grey to orange; the header shows "Mikro bereit".

The interface is German only and the tester found no language switch, so he could not make English screenshots. The developer says it is German only so far because the local version is optimised for German (vendor-claim).

A Meetings tab offers "Meeting aufnehmen"; its tip says calls give a transcript, summary and tasks and everything stays on the Mac. The tester has not recorded a meeting and plans to try it with a few people in a room.
The sprich.ai account page offers a password change and two-factor authentication. The 2FA card shows an "Aktivieren" link, so it is off.

A "Bug melden" form has Bug, Feedback and Feature tabs and fields for title, description, expected and actual result, frequency and up to 3 attachments of 1 MB each. The "Mitgesendete Daten" section was not opened and whether anything was sent is not recorded. The tester calls it impressive (tester-view). "Transcripts are never sent" is a vendor-claim.
The welcome screen and setup say everything runs locally, that voice and text never leave the Mac and that the app works fully offline. No network traffic was inspected and no offline run was tried.

Not tested or not recorded: file transcription and the dictionary tab (both visible in the navigation), the effect of the rewrite menu and the tone setting, dictation into Mail, Notes, Slack or a browser, plan and pricing, runtime memory, uninstall.
severity_note: Severity is the impact on a first-time user. Proposed, not measured. Info marks a finding that is neither a problem nor a strength; Positive marks something that worked well.

fits: German-speaking Mac users on Apple Silicon who dictate German or English into everyday apps and want the processing local, as the app states (assumption from one session).
not_fits: Anyone who needs Russian or a non-German interface today, or an Intel Mac (the directory lists Apple Silicon only).
audience.retest: Retest on a new major version, a published English interface or confirmed language list. Cover: record the app and macOS versions; time the delay; Russian with the language set; file transcription; Meetings; the rewrite menu; offline use with traffic inspected; runtime memory; uninstall.
